financial_anchor.value: $200.6bn net sales, up 20% year on year; $27.5bn operating income, up 43%; segment economics differ sharply between AWS, advertising and stores
financial_anchor.caveat: Reported/adjusted measures differ; cycle, mix and capital intensity confound.

ai_claim.claim: retail recommendation, forecasting and robotic fulfillment are established ML in the baseline.
ai_claim.scope: Specific workflow only; infrastructure demand is separated from own productivity.
ai_claim.limitation: No representative controlled cohort or retained-cash reconciliation.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: AI infrastructure growth requires very large capex and power.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Does not itself disprove the scoped mechanism.

rights_limit: Public terms do not prove universal training or pooled cross-customer reuse; enterprise schedules were unavailable.
materiality_summary: Framework convention: $6–7bn annual operating benefit, about 5% of a normalized operating-profit scale near the current run rate. Illustrative assumptions produce negative $0.31bn, below the hurdle.

arithmetic.inputs: pool $45bn eligible fulfillment, customer-service and corporate cost; efficiency 15%; realization 50%; retained share 50%; recurring cost $2.0bn
arithmetic.formula: eligible cost × efficiency × realization × retained share − recurring AI expense

g2_provisional: Watch/incomplete: E1–E2 route exists; no E3 quality-adjusted proof or E4 cash.
unresolved_questions: Eligible workload and matched quality KPI?
Retained economics after labor, model and capital costs?
